items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Put Mel Lewis up in front... Mel Lewis is dead... Richie Kamuca is dead, Mel Lewis is dead... when I put the band together... Med Flory, Frank Capp. When they make me an offer I can’t refuse. Because they’ve been with me for forty years

ctx.x: She was and old time movie columnist who could make you or break you, you know, in the movie business. She’d be sitting there. It didn’t make any sense that people were coming to see the band. And we were the heroes. We played — $15 a night and our bar tabs were $23. You’ve got to be an idiot to do that. We were having so much fun. We didn’t care about the music. And that went on for about five weeks in a row. It was Mondays, maybe two nights a week. Then the club owner says, “Why don’t we do this five nights a…

tell you what I need now.” I’m the band leader, there was something I wanted to hear. You know, right or wrong, I wanted to hear something that I wanted. It started with, “You hear how the lead trumpet player, how you can hear him so well?” “Yeah.” I said, “Now let me hear the fourth trumpet player. All four trumpets. On the same level.” I wanted to hear the sound of a band, not protruding notes. Now great, now you hear? In the old days, by the way, it was hard to record the bass. All you heard was boom-boom-…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’m talking about the big band, the Dream Band... everybody in the band was — by the end of the night he was 125. I was wishing him a Happy Birthday every fourth tune.

ctx.x: Yeah. You seem to have sensed, over the years, what kind of guidelines or maybe restrictions to put on the people you were leading. In other words you tolerated certain behaviors but not others.

Yeah. You couldn’t make any kind of hard dope like that. You could smoke pot. And no smoking at all on stage. I’m talking about the big band, the Dream Band, with the big band. But you can put your cognac underneath the what-do-you-call-it, the stand. I allowed that. Because what I would do is ‘cause I always, I never drank off stage. Never drank off stage. But on stage I was the Dean Martin of the vibes. I would have a cognac. I would drink cognac and I would always say, “Ladies and gentlemen, Mel Lewis has a…

Covid, if you don’t get your shots you’re liable to give it to somebody else. You know. Here, if you couldn’t play you’d be hanging up the guy sitting next to you playing his part. You know? If you weren’t playing, if it wasn’t together it could throw you off.
